venturebeat.com/security/the-three-layer.excerpt: Presented by Nutanix Autonomous systems that can reason, make their own decisions, and execute actions across an environment introduce a category of risk that application-level controls were never built to contain. Treating that risk as a single problem produces incomplete architectures, says Oscar Wahlberg, senior director of product management at Nutanix. "The guardrails to catch a malicious prompt won't stop an agent from hallucinating and doing something it never should have done, like accidentally deleting databases or leaking sensitive data with a credential it was granted but then uses for something entirely different," Wahlberg says. "That's the central problem as enterprises move autonomous agents out of experimentation and into production." Once an agentic system is granted execution privileges across the data center, the security posture has to scale into a defense-in-depth architecture spanning infrastructure, storage, compute, networking, and a governing control plane. Each layer addresses a distinct category of risk, rather than duplicating the same controls across the stack. No single security control or vendor can provide that protection on its own. Defense-in-depth depends on those layers working together. By dividing the responsibilities across the stack and adhering to zero trust segmentation, organizations can create a secure framework that improves their overall posture. Understanding which risks belong in each layer is what turns the principle of defense-in-depth into a practical security framework, with three layers that each have a distinct responsibility. venturebeat.com/orchestration/meta-resea.title: Meta researchers taught an 8B AI model to match Claude Opus 4.5 — without the frontier price tag
venturebeat.com/orchestration/meta-resea.excerpt: Consider an AI agent tasked with a complex enterprise workflow like migrating massive batches of customer records from a legacy CRM to a cloud database. The agent cannot rely solely on its internal context window for a job spanning hours and depends on the runtime layer, aka the harness . This harness provides execution feedback, like server logs, to help the agent maintain an accurate understanding of dynamic API connections. It also provides state trackers and control-flow mechanisms to manage completed and pending subgoals, ensuring the agent doesn't skip or duplicate data batches. When unexpected errors occur, such as a database rejecting a batch due to strict API rate limits, the harness provides tools and instructions to help the agent recover. The main way to tell an agent how and when to use its tools is to have a human developer write a set of rules and instructions telling it what to do step-by-step. For example, a developer might instruct the agent to always search the company wiki before writing an email. Because the agent is just following a rigid script, it lacks true autonomy. It hasn't been trained to independently weigh the costs and benefits of its actions. macrumors.com/2026/08/28/steve-jobs-scie.excerpt: A science project that Apple co-founder Steve Jobs built for his 8th-grade science fair sold at auction for $34,375. Jobs was attending Cupertino Jr. High when he designed the project, which is titled "What is the SCR?" The lot includes a display board built from plywood with three explanatory panels and a 10-page report with the same title. The left panel has a wooden model of a "typical silicon-controlled rectifier with its four alternate layers of P- and N-Type semiconductor material," while the center test circuits demonstrate the basic principles and characteristics of the silicon-controlled rectifier, as well as how it is most widely used. The right panel has a diagram and description of a 25-amp silicon-controlled rectifier. The project is labeled with Jobs' name, and the accompanying report is titled "What is the Silicon-Controlled Rectifier by Steve Jobs, Science, Mrs. Yakel, Feb. 29, 1968." A note included on the project instructs judges to plug in Circuit II and the oscilloscope to see it operate, and it asks them to "please unplug!" the device after testing it. Jobs' science fair project came from John Chovanec, Jobs' stepbrother. Chovanec's mother, Marilyn, married Paul Jobs in 1990 and continued to live in the Jobs family home in Los Altos. After Paul Jobs died in 1993, Steve Jobs declined to collect some of his personal belongings that remained in the home. Chovanec apparently asked Jobs to collect the items several times and at one point said he would keep the items himself instead. "Fine, but I don't want to be bothered about it again," Jobs reportedly responded. Chovanec previously sold other items from Jobs' early years, including posters, magazines, bow ties, a desk, and more. A 1977 Apple Computer poster sold for $659,900, while an Apple–1 Byte Shop wooden case owned by Jobs sold for $254,375. The bow ties sold for $113,580. m6_chip_announcement.headline: Apple Rolls Out M6‑Powered Macs, Skips M6 Pro and Max
m6_chip_announcement.summary: Apple’s new Mac mini launches with the first 2‑nm M6 chip, while most higher‑end Macs will retain M5 processors until the M7 family arrives.
highlights: Mac mini is the first Mac to feature the **M6** chip.
Entry‑level 14‑inch **MacBook Pro** and 24‑inch **iMac** are slated for **M6** updates in late 2026.
Apple will not produce **M6 Pro** or **M6 Max**, accelerating the rollout of **M7 Pro** and **M7 Max** in 2027.
High‑end models like **MacBook Ultra** will continue using **M5 Pro/Max** chips until the **M7** series launches.
The **M6** uses a new **2‑nanometer** process with a 12‑core CPU, 12‑core GPU and up to **170GB/s** memory bandwidth.

teams_scam_china.headline: Microsoft Teams Becomes a Scam Magnet in China as Victims Lose Up to $220,000
teams_scam_china.summary: Scammers in China are exploiting Microsoft Teams to run romance and investment frauds, leaving victims with losses ranging from $1,500 to $220,000.
highlights: Victims report losing between $1,500 and $300,000 after scammers hand them Teams login credentials
Local law enforcement has labeled Teams a “fraud‑related app” and issued public warnings
Microsoft added a warning banner in June and discontinued the personal Teams version in China

parse_5_release.headline: Cohere Parse 5 Cuts Document‑Parsing Costs While Lagging Behind Top AI Models
parse_5_release.summary: Cohere Parse 5, a 2.3‑billion‑parameter vision‑language model, offers enterprise‑scale PDF parsing at $1.50 per 1,000 pages, though it trails GPT‑5.5, Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.5 Flash in accuracy.
highlights: Parse 5 scores 79.2 on ParseBench, below GPT‑5.5 (84.4) and Opus 4.8 (84.3)
Pricing is $1.50 per 1,000 pages via Cohere API and Model Vault
Supports nine languages with stable accuracy and returns structured Markdown with HTML tables
Available through Microsoft Foundry, AWS SageMaker and Cohere’s secure Model Vault

self_improving_ai_research.headline: Anthropic's Automated Alignment Researcher Beats Human Experts, Cuts Costs to $4/hr
self_improving_ai_research.summary: Anthropic unveiled an Automated Alignment Researcher that improves alignment benchmarks faster than human researchers, achieving results in six hours at a fraction of the cost.
highlights: Automated system improved performance on all ten alignment benchmarks without degrading overall performance
The AAR method outperformed experienced human researchers on average within six hours
Cost per hour dropped from $150 for human researchers to roughly $4 for the AAR

vpn_privacy_risk_study.headline: Millions of US VPN Users Unwittingly Expose Data as 85% of Apps Hide Trackers, Proton Warns
vpn_privacy_risk_study.summary: A new Proton VPN study finds that 85% of mobile VPN apps in US stores contain hidden trackers, with 64 apps actively logging users' GPS locations.
highlights: 85% of US VPN apps contain hidden trackers
64 apps track physical GPS locations
Over 13.2 million downloads in June 2026 were of these risky apps
Chinese‑owned VPNs accounted for more than 3 million US downloads
Tracker data is sent to entities in Israel, China and Russia

anthropic_alignment_report.headline: Anthropic’s Claude Agents Auto‑Mitigate Ten AI Alignment Failures
anthropic_alignment_report.summary: Anthropic demonstrated that Claude‑powered agents can autonomously devise training methods that close safety gaps on ten alignment failures, outperforming human researchers at lower cost.
highlights: AARs built on Claude Opus 4.8 iterated for up to 48 hours, using a fixed H200 GPU budget.
The agents closed more safety gap than 28 seasoned human safety researchers on all tested failures.
Each AAR run cost roughly $4 per hour versus $150 per hour for human experts.
Methods generalized to larger models and unseen benchmarks, staying effective on models up to 4.7× scale.

search_ai_overlay.headline: Google Auto‑Expands AI Overviews, Pushing Traditional Search Links Down
search_ai_overlay.summary: Google now automatically expands AI Overviews for certain queries, placing a full AI summary and an “Ask anything” box above the regular list of results.
highlights: AI Overviews automatically expand for some queries, showing a full summary at the top of the page
The traditional list of links is moved farther down, often requiring extra scrolling
Google says the dynamic expansion is triggered when its systems deem it most useful for users

court_rules_pentagon_cant_ban_anthropic_.headline: Federal Court Overturns Pentagon Ban on Anthropic’s Claude AI Model
court_rules_pentagon_cant_ban_anthropic_.summary: A U.S. District Court ruled the Pentagon’s prohibition of Anthropic’s Claude illegal, dismissing the department’s legal arguments and restoring the model’s federal use.
highlights: Judge Rita Lin declared the ban illegal and baseless
The Defense Department had labeled Anthropic a supply‑chain risk in 2025
Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei criticized AI‑enabled surveillance and autonomous weapons
President Donald Trump had previously barred agencies from using Claude

glm_5_3_release.headline: Z.ai Unveils GLM‑5.3 Weights Under New $10 B Revenue‑Based License
glm_5_3_release.summary: Z.ai released the GLM‑5.3 model weights on Hugging Face, but only companies with over $10 billion in annual revenue can host it after passing a security review.
highlights: GLM‑5.3 weights are now downloadable from Hugging Face under a custom license
Companies exceeding $10 B revenue must clear Z.ai’s security review to deploy the model
The license replaces the previous MIT terms, tightening commercial use conditions

invest_bangladesh_act_2026_launch.headline: Bangladesh Launches Invest Bangladesh, Unifying Three Investment Agencies
invest_bangladesh_act_2026_launch.summary: Bangladesh merged BIDA, BEZA and PPPA into the new Invest Bangladesh agency to streamline licences, approvals and public‑private partnership processes under the Prime Minister’s Office.
highlights: Invest Bangladesh consolidates economic zones, free‑trade zones and industrial areas under one framework.
The agency will implement a 14‑day business licensing system and maintain the BanglaBiz digital platform.

import_policy_order_2026_29.headline: Bangladesh Opens Import Rules, Expands Free‑of‑Cost Facilities for Exporters
import_policy_order_2026_29.summary: The new Import Policy Order 2026‑29 removes LC limits, widens free‑of‑cost imports and sets FTZ guidelines to boost trade as Bangladesh prepares for post‑LDC status.
highlights: Annual ceiling on commercial imports without an LC is abolished, allowing unlimited contract‑based purchases.
FoC import limits for garment samples and trims are doubled to support export diversification.
First regulatory framework for FTZs and central bonded warehouses aims to attract foreign investment.

additional_350_million_lng_guarantee.headline: World Bank to Boost Bangladesh LNG Imports with $350 Million Guarantee
additional_350_million_lng_guarantee.summary: Bangladesh expects a new $350 million World Bank guarantee in November, doubling its LNG import facility to $700 million and easing foreign‑exchange pressure.
highlights: Total guarantee facility will rise to $700 million, with $650 million available via standby letters of credit.
The facility includes a $50 million credit support line and can be reused after payments are settled.
Petrobangla has already drawn about $235 million of the $250 million long‑term LNG allocation.

wall_street_ends_lower_after_fed_chair_w.headline: Wall Street Slides as Fed Chair Warsh Signals More Rate Hikes Ahead
wall_street_ends_lower_after_fed_chair_w.summary: Investors pulled back on Friday as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned that inflation remains above target, raising odds of a September rate increase.
highlights: Dow fell 0.02% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.25% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.52%
PayPal shares tumbled after a consortium abandoned its takeover bid
Gap shares rose on an upgraded profit outlook and a new Old Navy CEO

us_hits_egyptian_bank_branches_with_iran.headline: US sanctions Egyptian bank branches over Iran ties as war hits six months
us_hits_egyptian_bank_branches_with_iran.summary: The United States imposed Iran‑related sanctions on Banque Misr’s UAE branches, cutting them off from dollar transactions to pressure Tehran amid the six‑month war.
highlights: Treasury called the UAE branches a critical node for Iran’s dollar access
Secondary sanctions threaten countries that maintain business ties with Iran
The move targets Banque Misr’s operations in the United Arab Emirates

shanghai_plans_subsidies_to_kick_start_d.headline: Shanghai Announces Subsidies to Revive Dormant Offshore FTZ Bond Market
shanghai_plans_subsidies_to_kick_start_d.summary: Shanghai will offer subsidies to offshore issuers and allow onshore banks to purchase FTZ bonds, aiming to attract foreign investors and boost the free‑trade zone debt market.
highlights: The city will subsidise offshore issuers of FTZ bonds to lower financing costs.
The People’s Bank of China will permit onshore banks to buy FTZ bonds within a set quota.
